rubrics.rubric: Does the Current Grades sheet correctly calculate and present every student's Week 11 standing?
criterion: All 35 enrolled students appear once.
The sheet contains the eleven required columns in the instructed order.
Participation_Avg uses Weeks 1-11 and excludes blank cells from its denominator.
A recorded participation score of zero remains in the denominator.
An L or E attendance code changes the participation denominator only when the corresponding participation score is absent.
Quiz 1, Quiz 2, and Writing Assignment 1 percentages use their source-score maxima.
Weighted_Total uses the completed-work weights for Participation, Quiz 1, Quiz 2, and Writing Assignment 1.
Projected_Grade_Pct equals Weighted_Total divided by 0.65.
Letter grades use the scale supplied in the instructions.
Each Discrepancy_Flag identifies the week and nature of every attendance-versus-participation mismatch for that student.
Blank discrepancy cells or the word None are used only when no mismatch exists.

rubrics.rubric: Does the At-Risk Analysis identify all students meeting the stated rules and provide source-grounded, individualized interventions?
criterion: A student is included when Projected_Grade_Pct is below 70%.
A student is included when Attendance_Pct is below 60%.
A student is included when at least two completed-work score cells are missing under a stated interpretation of missing assignment scores.
Criteria_Triggered lists every rule met by the student.
Office-hours dates and reasons are reported from the Office Hours Log.
Active, Partial, and No Contact are applied using the definitions in the instructions.
The analysis states an as-of date consistent with a Week 11 mid-November review.
Office-hours entries after the stated review date are excluded or clearly labeled as post-review information.
Each intervention addresses the student's specific grade, attendance, or missing-work risks.
Each intervention reflects the student's prior engagement level and office-hours history.
Disability-accommodation history is handled as a support and implementation issue rather than as a negative compliance inference.

rubrics.rubric: Does Appeal_Decisions.docx adjudicate all four pending appeals with the required components and evidence?
criterion: All four appeals in the Grade Appeals sheet receive a separate decision section.
Each section identifies the student by name and ID.
Each section states the contested assignment and original score.
Each section reproduces or faithfully summarizes the stated appeal reason.
Each section includes short, accurately attributed excerpts from the applicable syllabus policy or Berkeley rubric criteria.
Each section uses Approved, Denied, or Partially Approved.
Each section gives a detailed rationale tied to the named inputs.
Each section reports an adjusted score or No change.
Quiz and participation appeals cross-reference relevant attendance, participation, and office-hours evidence.
The writing appeal evaluates the available work evidence against the cited rubric dimensions without inventing unseen essay content.
No particular appeal outcome is required when the ruling is supported by the cited evidence and documented uncertainty.

rubrics.rubric: Do the appeal decisions apply the relevant policies and external rubric accurately?
criterion: Quiz appeals use the syllabus rules for quiz timing, approved extensions, prior communication, and case-by-case make-ups as applicable.
The disability-accommodation appeal considers the syllabus exception for an approved extension and the documented accommodation history.
The participation appeal distinguishes an explicit zero from a missing participation score.
The participation appeal considers the asynchronous PlayPosit course format when assessing a claimed Zoom attendance event.
The writing appeal cites the Berkeley Originality performance levels or faithful equivalents.
The writing appeal also considers the other Berkeley dimensions relevant to an analytical essay score.
The required quoted source excerpts are attributed to the correct syllabus or Berkeley document; paraphrase may supplement but does not replace those excerpts.
Later-dated office-hours entries are not treated as evidence of conduct before the stated review date unless labeled as retrospective context.

rubrics.rubric: Does Quiz3_Assessment_Blueprint.csv map Weeks 9-14 to the official CLEP content framework?
criterion: The CSV contains Week, Topic, CLEP_Category, CLEP_Subtopic, and CLEP_Weight_Pct columns.
Every syllabus topic from Weeks 9-14 appears in at least one mapping row.
Each topic is mapped to a defensible CLEP category and subtopic.
Cross-cutting topics may use more than one mapping row when the rationale is clear.
Institutions rows use the official 20% category weight.
Social Patterns rows use the official 15% category weight.
Social Processes rows use the official 20% category weight.
Social Stratification rows use the official 30% category weight.
The Sociological Perspective rows use the official 15% category weight.
The file does not replace the official category weights with a locally reweighted quiz allocation.

rubrics.rubric: Does Quiz3_Study_Guide.docx provide a CLEP-organized guide and five weighted sample questions?
criterion: The guide is organized by CLEP category rather than by course week.
The guide covers the Weeks 9-14 topics represented in the blueprint.
Each topic includes relevant key concepts.
The guide contains exactly five multiple-choice sample questions.
Each sample question includes an answer.
Each sample question is labeled with its CLEP category.
The five-question allocation reasonably reflects the official weights across categories covered by the course topics; a nearest-integer allocation does not require a separate rounding explanation.

rubrics.rubric: Does the submission provide the complete academic review package with consistent student data and source use?
criterion: The output includes SOC101_Midterm_Report.xlsx, Appeal_Decisions.docx, Quiz3_Assessment_Blueprint.csv, and Quiz3_Study_Guide.docx.
The workbook contains Current Grades and At-Risk Analysis sheets.
Student names, IDs, scores, attendance values, and office-hours records are consistent across the workbook and appeal decisions.
CLEP category labels and weights are consistent between the blueprint and study guide.
The package distinguishes source facts from analyst assumptions or unresolved evidence.
The syllabus, Berkeley rubric, and CLEP fact sheet are identified when their policies, criteria, or weights are used.
